clue.text: Produce beer, say, leading to laughter and commotion

indicators.note: say tells us to take the phrase as it is spoken, not as it is written

parts.note: to produce beer is to brew it
ha-ha is the sound of laughter

explanation.surface: Brewing beer, it is claimed, leads to laughter and then a noisy commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks BROU as spoken like BREW; the French-derived spelling is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy fuss or uproar, a synonym for a commotion.

clue.text: On one's own, extremely sad without wife

parts.note: so can mean extremely, as in so happy

indicators.note: without means the letter for wife is dropped from the word

parts.note: low means sad or depressed

explanation.surface: Someone left alone is very sad now their wife has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops W from LOW, leaving LO. SOLO is also OSLO rearranged, one of the theme's capitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Solo means alone, done by one person with no companion.

clue.text: Strange animal from a land in Africa

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of the next word are made odd, rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd creature hails from an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges ANIMAL. The answer is also an anagram of MANILA, a theme capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Malian is the adjective for Mali, a country in West Africa.

clue.text: Put in flap provided with fabric covering

indicators.note: covering means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: terry is a looped cotton towelling fabric
if means provided, as in on condition that

explanation.surface: Someone tucks a flap in and covers it with cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone in a flap means to scare them badly, which is what terrify means.

clue.text: Source of poison for barbs, as repute has spread

indicators.note: has spread suggests the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A rumour about a source of arrow poison has spread around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has spread' rearranges AS REPUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas tree of Java has a toxic sap traditionally used to poison arrow tips.

clue.text: For some diners, it's still an alternative to alcohol

definitions.text: For some diners, it's still an alternative to alcohol

parts.words: For some diners, it's still an alternative to alcohol
parts.note: still is a pun: a non-sparkling bottled drink served at restaurants, as opposed to wine

explanation.walkthrough: 'still' reads as 'yet', but it means not fizzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottled mineral water served with meals is offered still or sparkling instead of wine.

clue.text: Isn't missing any piggies in rush

parts.note: someone who isn't missing something has it
piggies is a nursery word for toes, of which there are ten, so having ten means none missing

explanation.surface: A child in a hurry hasn't lost any toes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This little piggy' is a nursery rhyme counted on the toes. The answer also rearranges to ATHENS, a theme capital.
explanation.definitionFit: To hasten is to hurry or rush.

clue.text: Following priest, I make a speech in religious office

indicators.note: following puts the rest of the pieces after the priest

parts.note: to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: After the priest, someone delivers a sermon in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A priorate is the office or term of a prior, a religious post.

clue.text: Square loaf mostly consumed by father

indicators.note: consumed by means the second piece goes inside the father

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: to loaf is to laze about

explanation.surface: A father has eaten most of a square loaf of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts LAZE to LAZ. 'loaf' looks like bread but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is an open public square in a town.

clue.text: Wrestler having problem with ring

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A wrestler struggles with something in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' suits wrestling but just gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is Japanese wrestling, used here for one of its wrestlers.

clue.text: Showing hesitation that could make one loser? True

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: could make says the letters may be rebuilt into a new word

explanation.surface: An indecisive person might call themselves a loser, and agree it is true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges I, LOSER and TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being irresolute means wavering and unable to decide.

clue.text: In South America, revolutionary movement got US rocket

parts.note: a turn is a movement of revolution, as of a wheel

explanation.surface: A Latin American uprising acquired an American missile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests politics in South America, but here a turn is a rotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn was the NASA rocket family that launched the Apollo missions.

clue.text: Like toss of coin, uncertain

definitions.meaning: a tossed coin spins while airborne

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes a flipped coin and figuratively means undecided.

clue.text: Gave up? Fine, we're not upset

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: upset suggests the letters are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off quitting, saying it's fine and they're not upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges F with WERENOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Forwent, past of forgo, means went without or gave something up.

clue.text: I and others going astray in a dozen other answers

definitions.text: I and others going astray in a dozen other answers

parts.words: I and others going astray in a dozen other answers
parts.note: I is an upper-case letter; also the theme's cities lose their letter order in other answers

explanation.walkthrough: Answers such as SOLO, MORE, MAIL, HASTEN and GEARUP are rearranged national cities.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper-case letters such as I, and also the letters of chief cities, as the theme shows.

clue.text: Line in a statement of obvious selflessness

indicators.note: in places the line inside the following words

parts.note: a truism is a statement of the obvious

explanation.surface: A line about obvious generosity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L between A and TRUISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Altruism is unselfish concern for others, i.e. selflessness.

clue.text: See 15
Made better in course of cure? For me, definitely

indicators.note: in the course of means the letters run through the following words

explanation.surface: A patient says the treatment is certainly working for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in course of' finds the letters across CURE FOR ME DEFINITELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Reformed means improved or amended.

clue.text: Piece of Internet address shortly providing logical system

parts.note: .org is a domain suffix in web addresses
anon is an old word meaning soon or shortly

explanation.surface: A fragment of a web address gives a system of logic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' looks like an abbreviation signal but means ANON.
explanation.definitionFit: Organon is Aristotle's set of logical works, hence a system of reasoning.

clue.text: It creates a stir when a reptile swallows it

indicators.note: swallows means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: gator is short for alligator
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something causes a fuss when a crocodile-like creature gulps it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' is the container signal; 'It' at the start is part of the definition, the device that stirs.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator stirs up trouble, and also a device that stirs liquid.

clue.text: Get prepared for a purge after revolution

indicators.note: after a revolution things are overturned and reordered

explanation.surface: Ready yourself for a purge once the coup is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revolution' rearranges A PURGE. The answer also rearranges to PRAGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To gear up is to get ready or equip oneself.

clue.text: Powerless to control one import

parts.note: a means one
drift means the gist or import of something

explanation.surface: Someone cannot stop a single item coming in.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat adrift has no means of steering, so is helpless.

clue.text: Part of flower showing love from somebody else

indicators.note: from here means taken away from

parts.note: another means somebody else
O is love, nil in tennis

explanation.surface: A flower shows love from some other admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes O out of ANOTHER. The answer rearranges to TEHRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The anther is the pollen-bearing tip of a stamen.

clue.text: Non-alcoholic drink at AA, if clue is deciphered

indicators.note: deciphering a code rearranges letters into sense

explanation.surface: An Alcoholics Anonymous drink, once the clue is worked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is deciphered' rearranges AT AA IF CLUE. AA is Alcoholics Anonymous.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee with milk, a drink without alcohol.

clue.text: One part of me wanted second helping

annotationWithheld.why: One part of me wanted second helping (4): MORE is the definition 'second helping', but no parse of 'One part of me wanted' found giving MORE
annotationWithheld.clue: One part of me wanted second helping

clue.text: Post providing protection for old warrior

definitions.meaning: letters sent through the postal service
chain armour worn by medieval knights

explanation.definitionFit: Mail means both postal letters and chain armour.

clue.text: Multinational group and that entity's components

parts.note: UN is the United Nations
it's is a contraction of it is

explanation.surface: A global body and its parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer rearranges to TUNIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Units are the single parts making up a whole.

clue.text: Short crack found aboard English vessel

parts.note: on means aboard
E is English
a liner is a passenger ship

explanation.surface: A small fracture found on board an English ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' is a joke, not a split in the hull.
explanation.definitionFit: A quip delivered in a single line is a short joke.
